page: Google Cloud Platform a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is an accelerator-optimized bare-metal-equivalent virtual instance designed for massive distributed compute workloads. It combines 8 NVIDIA Hopper H200 GPUs providing a combined 1,128 GB of VRAM with an x86_64 host system powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. The host features 224 dedicated vCPUs across 112 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.1 GHz, backed by 260 MB of L3 cache and support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). System memory totals 2,952 GB of RAM, offering roughly 13.18 GB per vCPU.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory bandwidth. The machine achieved top-tier standing in stress-ng multi-core testing (180,184.5) and PassMark overall CPU rating (125,594.41), augmented by strong Geekbench multi-core results. Memory bandwidth reaches 431.26 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and over 13,946 GB/sec for cached transfers. High-concurrency data benchmarks highlight its capabilities, recording 221.56 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 209.03 GB/sec in static serving throughput. Single-core performance falls in the average tier across stress-ng and compression tasks, reflecting a topology optimized for aggregate parallel execution rather than serial clock speed.

A key architectural consideration for the a3-ultragpu-8g-nolssd is the absence of bundled local NVMe storage. Workloads requiring local disk scratch space must rely on networked storage options, which shifts IOPS dependencies to the cloud fabric. From a resource perspective, the instance packs substantial compute density per node, optimizing resource overhead for distributed deep learning operations. The configuration fits large language model training, multi-GPU AI model fine-tuning, large-scale scientific simulations, and distributed in-memory data processing pipelines.
